title: “Crypto, MLMs—I keep falling for get-rich-quick schemes”
channel: I Will Teach You To Be Rich
summary: A money coach confronts a high-earning couple deep in debt who keep chasing MLMs, timeshares and 0% balance-transfer tricks, and pushes them to cut fixed costs, stop chasing points and invest automatically.

assertions.quote: everything you do with your money is centered around get rich quick and schemes and gimmicks

verdicts.note: Each scheme carries upfront costs and most lose money, so the pattern compounds into debt; this is consistent with consumer-finance research on scheme victims.

In the sports-betting setting only: constrained households that gain betting access raise credit card balances, lose available credit, cut card payments and overdraw more, so they become more indebted rather than merely reallocating funds.

MLM participants were significantly more likely to have declared bankruptcy than non-participants (18% vs 11%), with 72% of those bankruptcies after MLM involvement; the authors note causality cannot be established, and this covers MLM only.

assertions.quote: they are not worth tens of thousands of dollars in debt just so you can get a $235 free flight

verdicts.note: Points are worth about a cent each while revolving interest runs 20 to 30 percent a year, so any carried balance wipes out the rewards many times over.

assertions.quote: anytime you find yourself talking about playing a game a gimmick a hack like 0% balance transfers that's a gimmick

verdicts.note: Transfers carry fees and promotional rates expire; research on balance-transfer users shows many end up with the same or larger balances.

assertions.quote: the mlms time share time share it goes on and on

verdicts.note: Timeshares depreciate immediately, carry rising maintenance fees and have almost no resale market; consumer regulators treat exit scams as a direct consequence.

assertions.quote: you have a very small chance of winning when you go up against multi-billion doll companies

verdicts.note: Card issuers design rewards and promotional offers around revolver behaviour; their profitability depends on most customers not winning the game.

assertions.quote: we're not hoping for the next big thing to come around the corner there is no secret money coming in this is it
when I'm down I usually just go on Amazon and buy a bunch of stuff because it makes me feel better

verdicts.note: Compulsive buying is a recognised behavioural pattern with evidence for cognitive-behavioural treatment, though structural changes to accounts also help.
